balanced.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.85, chunked_prefill_size 8192, schedule_policy lpm (serve requests whose beginning is cached first) and max_running_requests 32. Everything else stays at SGLang's own choices for your card.
balanced.example: 0.85 with 90 GB free keeps about 13.5 GB as headroom.
balanced.risks: A card shared with another engine needs a lower fraction; 0.85 keeps 15 % of the free memory for working room, which is plenty on most cards but not for very long prompts on a tight setup.
balanced.summary: A safe all-round start: 85 % of the free memory, 8,192-token prompt chunks, cache-aware scheduling and up to 32 conversations.
balanced.when_to_change: Choose it when you are unsure, and adjust one thing at a time from here.

long-context.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.85, chunked_prefill_size 4096 so reading a huge prompt in small pieces needs little temporary memory, kv_cache_dtype fp8_e4m3 to roughly double the tokens that fit, at most 4 conversations at once and lpm scheduling. The window itself comes from the model or your context_length setting.
long-context.example: Asking questions about a 300-page report pasted into a single prompt.
long-context.risks: fp8 can cost a little answer quality. Few conversations fit at once, and the trtllm_mha prefill backend refuses an fp8_e4m3 cache on sm_120. Set context_length too if you want a window above the model's default.
long-context.summary: Fits very long documents with the KV cache stored in 8 bits, for a few conversations at a time.
long-context.when_to_change: Choose it to read whole books, long codebases or big logs in one prompt.

low-latency.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.80, chunked_prefill_size 2048, first come first served scheduling, at most 8 conversations at once and a stream interval of 1 (every token is sent right away). The lower memory fraction leaves more room for working buffers.
low-latency.example: A single developer chatting with a model and watching the answer stream in.
low-latency.risks: More than a handful of simultaneous users queue up, and the lower fraction leaves less cache, so fewer or shorter conversations fit.
low-latency.summary: Makes one or two users' answers start and stream as fast as possible, with small chunks and few conversations at once.
low-latency.when_to_change: Choose it for a personal assistant, a coding helper or a demo where response time matters more than capacity.

max-throughput.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.88, chunked_prefill_size 16384, max_prefill_tokens 32768, lpm scheduling, mixed prefill and decode batches, CUDA graphs up to 256 conversations (SGLang's own choice on 60 to 160 GB cards) and a stream interval of 8, which sends text in chunks of eight tokens to save CPU time.
max-throughput.example: A team assistant or an evaluation run that sends dozens of requests at once.
max-throughput.risks: Bigger chunks need more temporary memory, and 0.88 leaves less headroom, so long prompts can run out of memory on a tight card. Text appears in visible jumps of eight tokens.
max-throughput.summary: Serves as many users as possible at once, using bigger prompt chunks, mixed batches and rare streaming flushes.
max-throughput.when_to_change: Choose it for a shared service or batch jobs with many simultaneous requests.

reasoning.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.85, chunked_prefill_size 8192, lpm scheduling, reasoning_parser qwen3 and a watchdog timeout of 1,800 seconds so a long step is not mistaken for a hang. Thinking uses many tokens, so answers take longer and need more window.
reasoning.example: A math or planning question where the model works through steps before the final answer.
reasoning.risks: A parser for another family can swallow part of the answer or leave raw markup in it. A long watchdog delays the restart after a real hang.
reasoning.summary: Set up for models that think before they answer: the qwen3 reasoning parser and a long watchdog for slow steps.
reasoning.when_to_change: Choose it for Qwen3-style reasoning models; change the parser for other families.

tool-agent.details: Sets mem_fraction_static 0.85, chunked_prefill_size 8192, lpm scheduling (agents resend a growing history), up to 16 conversations at once, tool_call_parser qwen3_coder, reasoning_parser qwen3 and cached-token reports in usage. The parsers suit Qwen3.x models; other families need their own parser.
tool-agent.example: A coding agent that edits files and runs commands through tool calls.
tool-agent.risks: A parser that does not match the model leaves raw tool markup in the answer and agents stall; the Compatibility check warns about common mismatches.
tool-agent.summary: Set up for assistants that call tools, with the qwen3_coder tool parser, the qwen3 reasoning parser and cache reporting.
tool-agent.when_to_change: Choose it for coding agents or assistants with function calls on Qwen3.x-style models, and change both parsers otherwise.
